en.headline: Financial Secretary signals full-year GDP forecast will be raised
en.dek: Paul Chan said the economy expanded 5.1 per cent in the first half and authorities will revise the annual growth projection upward later this month.
body: Financial Secretary Paul Chan said in his weekly blog that the Hong Kong economy grew 5.1 per cent year on year in the first half of 2026 and that the Government will raise its full-year GDP growth forecast later this month.

The current official projection stands at 2.5 to 3.5 per cent. Chan said merchandise exports are expected to continue benefiting from strong global demand for artificial-intelligence-related products in the second half, while services exports should be supported by overseas demand for financial and business services and rising tourist arrivals.

He also noted that the first offshore Chinese government bond futures contract will debut in Hong Kong on Monday and pledged to further promote the global use of the renminbi. Chan cautioned that geopolitical developments, US interest rates and other uncertainties still warrant close monitoring.

zh.headline: 陳茂波：上半年經濟增長5.1% 稍後上調全年預測
zh.dek: 財政司司長陳茂波在網誌表示，本港上半年經濟按年增長5.1%，當局稍後本月內會上調全年本地生產總值增長預測。
body: 財政司司長陳茂波在最新網誌指出，本港經濟在2026年上半年按年實質增長5.1%，政府稍後本月內會上調全年經濟增長預測。
現時官方預測全年增長介乎2.5%至3.5%。陳茂波表示，下半年貨品出口料繼續受惠於全球對人工智能相關產品的強勁需求，而金融及專業服務的海外需求以及訪港旅客上升，亦會支持服務出口。
他同時提到，首隻離岸中國國債期貨合約將於周一在港推出，並重申會繼續推動人民幣國際化。陳茂波亦提醒，地緣政治發展、美國利率走勢及其他不確定因素仍需密切留意。
